_meta.title: HybridTurtle Rule Overlap Analysis
_meta.methodology: For each pair of rules acting on the same signal, assess: (1) whether they measure the same condition, (2) whether both are needed, (3) what data would prove redundancy. Recommendations are conservative — KEEP unless strong evidence to simplify.

verdicts.KEEP: Both rules serve distinct purposes and should remain
verdicts.RETEST: Overlap suspected but needs data to prove. Use filter scorecard / candidate outcome data to test.
verdicts.REDUCE: Evidence of redundancy. Consider removing one layer or softening thresholds.
verdicts.REMOVE_CANDIDATE: Strong evidence of redundancy. Mark for eventual removal after data validation.

overlaps.name: ADX Triple Layer
overlaps.description: ADX is checked 4 times: (1) SCAN-02 hard gate at ADX ≥ 20, (2) BQS-TREND gives continuous 0–25 pts for ADX 15–35, (3) FWS-MARGINAL penalizes ADX < 30 with up to 10 pts, (4) Weekly ADX gives ±5–10 pts bonus/penalty. After SCAN-02 blocks ADX < 20, FWS-MARGINAL still penalizes ADX 20–30 (which already passed the gate), and BQS-TREND gives a low score for the same candidates.
overlaps.reasoning: The gate + BQS bonus are clearly value-add (pass/fail + quality gradient). The question is whether FWS-MARGINAL adds information after SCAN-02 already filtered out ADX < 20. Weekly ADX is a different timeframe — intended.
overlaps.testPlan: Use filter scorecard: compare forward returns for candidates with ADX 20–25 vs 25–30 vs 30+. If 20–25 candidates perform as well as 25–30, FWS-MARGINAL may be too aggressive in the 20–30 zone.
overlaps.pruneSuggestion: If data shows ADX 20–30 candidates perform acceptably, reduce FWS-MARGINAL thresholds. E.g., only penalize ADX < 22 (instead of < 30).

overlaps.name: ATR/Volatility Triple Layer
overlaps.description: ATR is checked 4 times: (1) SCAN-04 hard cap at 8%/7%, (2) SCAN-08 spike detection at 1.3× median → demote/block, (3) BQS-VOLATILITY rewards sweet-spot ATR% (1–4%), (4) FWS-VOL-SHOCK penalizes spiking (+20 pts). A spiking stock is hit by SCAN-08 (demotion), FWS-VOL-SHOCK (-20 NCS), and potentially SCAN-04 if ATR% crosses the cap.
overlaps.reasoning: SCAN-08 and FWS-VOL-SHOCK use the same atrSpiking flag — double penalty. One blocks/demotes AND the other penalizes the score. This is the most clear-cut double-counting in the system.
overlaps.testPlan: Use candidate outcome data: compare outcomes of spike-demoted candidates. If the scan demotion already effectively filters them, the FWS penalty is redundant (candidates that pass despite SCAN-08 SOFT_CAP still get FWS-penalized).
overlaps.pruneSuggestion: Remove FWS-VOL-SHOCK for SOFT_CAP cases (bullish + spiking). Keep FWS penalty only for collapsing ATR (SCAN-08 doesn't handle that case as strongly).

overlaps.name: Earnings Triple Layer
overlaps.description: Earnings checked 3 times: (1) SCAN-10 hard blocks ≤2d or demotes 3–5d, (2) PENALTY-EARNINGS gives NCS 10–20 pt penalty, (3) ALLOC-EARNINGS gives allocation 5–10 pt penalty. A candidate 3 days from earnings gets: WATCH demotion + ~10 NCS penalty + ~5 allocation penalty. The NCS and allocation penalties reduce ranking of candidates that already can't be READY.
overlaps.reasoning: The scan block/demotion is the protective action. The NCS penalty further reduces score of already-demoted candidates. The allocation penalty then further demotes their capital priority. For ≤2d (already blocked), both penalties are wasted. For 3–5d (demoted to WATCH), the penalties are marginal since WATCH candidates rarely get traded.
overlaps.testPlan: Check how many 3–5d-from-earnings candidates actually get traded. If near zero, the NCS + allocation penalties are dead weight.
overlaps.pruneSuggestion: Keep SCAN-10 (protective action). Keep NCS penalty (affects scoring in backtest). Remove ALLOC-EARNINGS (allocation score already reflects NCS which includes the earnings penalty).

overlaps.name: Cluster Concentration Triple Layer
overlaps.description: Cluster exposure checked 3 times: (1) GATE-04 hard blocks above 25%, (2) PENALTY-CLUSTER penalizes NCS starting at 80% of cap, (3) ALLOC-CLUSTER penalizes allocation starting at 60% of cap. The allocation penalty kicks in earliest (60%), then NCS (80%), then gate (100%). This is a graduated response — soft warning → score reduction → hard block.
overlaps.reasoning: This is actually well-designed graduated deterrence. Each layer serves a distinct purpose: allocation deprioritizes, NCS warns, gate blocks. The thresholds don't fully overlap (60% / 80% / 100%). However, the PENALTY-CLUSTER and ALLOC-CLUSTER thresholds could be reconciled — both are soft penalties with different onset points.
overlaps.testPlan: Not needed for pruning — this is working as intended.
overlaps.pruneSuggestion: None. Consider harmonizing onset points if simplification is desired (both start at 70%).

overlaps.name: Anti-Chase + Extension + FWS Chasing
overlaps.signal: Price extended above entry trigger / recent highs
overlaps.description: Three rules detect 'candidate price has run too far': (1) SCAN-11 gap guard blocks on ATR/% thresholds, (2) SCAN-12 extension check blocks if > 0.8 ATR above trigger, (3) FWS-EXTENSION penalizes 15–25 pts for chasing 20d/55d highs. A gapped-up stock can be blocked by SCAN-11 or SCAN-12, AND get FWS-penalized by EXTENSION for the same price movement.
overlaps.reasoning: SCAN-11 and SCAN-12 are hard blocks at different thresholds (ATR/% gap vs 0.8 ATR extension). FWS-EXTENSION uses a different signal (chasing_20_last5 flags) but detects a similar condition. The overlap is partial because chasing flags measure multi-day extension while SCAN-11/12 measure single-day gaps.
overlaps.testPlan: Compare: when SCAN-11/12 block a candidate, does FWS-EXTENSION also fire? If co-occurrence > 80%, one penalty is redundant.
overlaps.pruneSuggestion: If data shows high co-occurrence, reduce FWS-EXTENSION weight from 25/15 to 15/10 since the hard blocks already handle the worst cases.

overlaps.name: DI Direction: Gate + Score
overlaps.description: SCAN-03 is a binary gate (+DI > −DI). BQS-DIRECTION gives 0–10 pts for the same DI spread. After the gate passes (spread > 0), BQS granulates the quality of the spread.
overlaps.reasoning: Classic gate + gradient pattern. The gate ensures minimum quality; the score differentiates within passing candidates. This is good design.

overlaps.name: Proximity: Classification + Score
overlaps.description: SCAN-09 classifies READY/WATCH/FAR by distance. BQS-PROXIMITY gives 0–15 pts for the same distance metric. Both use distance-to-high as input.
overlaps.reasoning: Same pattern as OVERLAP-06. Classification is pass/fail; score adds granularity. Good design.

overlaps.name: Hurst: Flag + Score
overlaps.description: SCAN-07 flags hurstWarn when H < 0.5. BQS-HURST gives 0–8 pts bonus for H > 0.5. The flag is advisory only (no blocking); the score adds quality differentiation.
overlaps.reasoning: complementary — flag warns operator, score affects ranking. Low overlap risk.

overlaps.name: Breadth Safety vs Max Positions Gate
overlaps.description: GATE-02 caps at 4 positions for SMALL_ACCOUNT. MOD-BREADTH caps at 4 when breadth < 40%. For SMALL_ACCOUNT, breadth safety never adds value because the profile already caps at 4.
overlaps.reasoning: For SMALL_ACCOUNT profile (4 max positions), Module 10 breadth safety's position cap is always redundant — it caps at the same number. The breadth percentage is still useful information, but the position override does nothing.
overlaps.testPlan: Verify: has MOD-BREADTH ever capped below what GATE-02 already caps? For SMALL_ACCOUNT, the answer is provably 'no'.
overlaps.pruneSuggestion: Remove the maxPositionsOverride from MOD-BREADTH for SMALL_ACCOUNT. Keep the breadth percentage display as informational.

overlaps.name: Volume: BQS Bonus vs FWS Penalty
overlaps.description: BQS rewards vol > 1.2 with 0–5 pts. FWS penalizes vol < 1.2 with 0–30 pts. These are complementary inverses, not duplicates.
overlaps.reasoning: Intentionally asymmetric: heavy penalty for low volume (up to 30 pts FWS) vs light bonus for high volume (up to 5 pts BQS). The asymmetry reflects that low volume is a bigger red flag than high volume is a green flag.

overlaps.name: Regime: BQS Direction vs FWS Stability
overlaps.description: BQS-REGIME scores regime direction (bearish -10, bullish +10–20). FWS-REGIME penalizes regime instability (+10 if not stable). These measure different dimensions: direction vs confidence.
overlaps.reasoning: Distinct signals. A bullish but unstable regime gets BQS bonus AND FWS penalty — the net effect is moderate (appropriate). Complementary design.

overlaps.name: Whipsaw vs Failed Breakout Cooldown
overlaps.description: SCAN-13 blocks 5 days after failed breakout. MOD-WHIPSAW blocks 60 days after 2+ stops in 30 days. Different triggers and different durations.
overlaps.reasoning: Different severity levels. Failed breakout is a short pause (5d). Whipsaw is a long pause (60d) for repeat offenders. Not redundant.

overlaps.name: Sector: Gate + Allocation
overlaps.description: GATE-05 blocks at sector cap (30%). ALLOC-SECTOR penalizes allocation score above 60% of cap. Graduated deterrence.
overlaps.reasoning: Same pattern as cluster triple layer but only dual layer. Gate blocks, score deprioritizes. Clean design.

mostSuspiciousOverlaps.name: ATR/Volatility Triple Layer
mostSuspiciousOverlaps.issue: ATR spike detection (SCAN-08) and FWS vol shock (FWS-VOL-SHOCK) use the same atrSpiking flag. A spiking stock gets blocked/demoted AND score-penalized. The FWS penalty is likely wasted on candidates already demoted.
mostSuspiciousOverlaps.impact: Score pollution — NCS of spiking candidates is artificially suppressed beyond what the scan demotion achieves.
mostSuspiciousOverlaps.actionRequired: Use candidate outcome data to verify. If spike-demoted candidates who barely pass still underperform, the FWS penalty adds value. If they don't, remove FWS-VOL-SHOCK for SOFT_CAP cases.

mostSuspiciousOverlaps.name: Earnings Triple Layer
mostSuspiciousOverlaps.issue: Earnings proximity is penalized 3 times: scan blocks, NCS penalizes, allocation penalizes. For ≤2d candidates (already blocked), the NCS + allocation penalties are dead weight. For 3–5d (demoted), the allocation penalty adds negligible value since NCS already includes an earnings penalty.
mostSuspiciousOverlaps.impact: Low practical impact since blocked candidates don't trade. Minor score distortion for 3–5d cases.
mostSuspiciousOverlaps.actionRequired: Remove ALLOC-EARNINGS penalty from allocation-score.ts. NCS earnings penalty + scan demotion already handle this.

mostSuspiciousOverlaps.name: Breadth Safety vs Max Positions
mostSuspiciousOverlaps.issue: Module 10 breadth safety caps positions at 4 when breadth < 40%. SMALL_ACCOUNT already caps at 4 via GATE-02. The breadth cap is provably redundant for this profile.
mostSuspiciousOverlaps.impact: Zero — the cap never fires because it matches the existing limit.
mostSuspiciousOverlaps.actionRequired: Safe to remove the position cap from breadth safety for SMALL_ACCOUNT. Keep breadth % as display-only.

mostSuspiciousOverlaps.name: ADX Triple Layer
mostSuspiciousOverlaps.issue: FWS-MARGINAL penalizes ADX 20–30 even though SCAN-02 already blocked ADX < 20 and BQS-TREND gives a low score for weak trends. The FWS penalty may be over-penalizing marginal-but-acceptable trends.
mostSuspiciousOverlaps.impact: Candidates with ADX 20–25 get: passed gate (barely), low BQS-TREND score, AND FWS penalty. Net: significantly deprioritized despite being valid trend-following setups.
mostSuspiciousOverlaps.actionRequired: Use score validation data: compare forward returns for ADX 20–25 vs 25–30 candidates. If ADX 20–25 performs well enough, reduce FWS-MARGINAL thresholds.

bestPruningCandidates.reason: NCS already includes earnings penalty. Allocation score uses NCS as quality input. Adding a separate allocation earnings penalty is triple-counting.
bestPruningCandidates.risk: Very low — allocation score still reflects earnings via NCS quality component.

bestPruningCandidates.reason: SMALL_ACCOUNT max position = 4, identical to breadth safety cap. Provably redundant.
bestPruningCandidates.risk: Zero for SMALL_ACCOUNT. Keep for other profiles where max positions > 4.
bestPruningCandidates.effort: Trivial — add profile check before applying position cap

bestPruningCandidates.reason: SCAN-08 already demotes spiking stocks (SOFT_CAP). FWS-VOL-SHOCK adds 20pts penalty on top. Consider reducing to 10 for SOFT_CAP cases.
bestPruningCandidates.risk: Medium — need data to confirm. If spiking stocks that pass SOFT_CAP still underperform, keep the penalty.
bestPruningCandidates.effort: Medium — requires changing FWS computation to be spike-action-aware

bestPruningCandidates.reason: ADX 20–25 already barely passed SCAN-02 and gets low BQS-TREND. FWS adds another 7 pts penalty. May over-penalize valid setups.
bestPruningCandidates.risk: Medium — changing this could let through weaker trends. Need data.
bestPruningCandidates.effort: Trivial — adjust threshold from 30 to 22 or 25
